rows.design: double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled; lesions on one side of the body treated, other side placebo (split-body)
rows.skin_tone: not in abstract (authors' affiliation is in Thailand; study site not stated)
rows.intervention: 0.1% tacrolimus ointment on lesions of one side of the body (frequency and total duration not in abstract)
rows.comparator: placebo ointment of the same physical appearance on lesions of the other side
rows.time_from_last_treatment: NOT_DERIVABLE: the abstract counts visits from the start of treatment ('at baseline and at 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 months of treatment') and describes no visit after treatment ended
rows.texture_or_scar: not in abstract (abstract calls the treatment 'safe' without listing adverse events)
rows.citation: Rerknimitr P, Disphanurat W, Achariyakul M. J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol 2013;27(4):460-464
rows.analysis_unit: side (treated side vs placebo side, colorimeter reading)
rows.endpoint_definition: mean luminosity scale adjusted for baseline (lower value = darker skin)
rows.arm_result: treated-side mean luminosity, adjusted for baseline, gradually decreased and was significantly different from the placebo side after 6 months of treatment (P = 0.019); size of the difference not in abstract
rows.uncertainty: No effect size, units or per-arm values in the abstract, only a P value. Unit of analysis (side, lesion or patient) not stated; the abstract says 'compared with the control group' although control is the other side of the same patients. Reading lower luminosity as darkening (repigmentation) is the standard colorimeter interpretation, not stated in the abstract. Treatment duration not stated, so whether the 6-month visit was the end of treatment is unknown.

rows.uncertainty: 11% is not a whole-number share of 26 patients (2/26 = [7.7%], 3/26 = [11.5%]); it fits 3/26 only if 11.5% was truncated, otherwise the evaluable denominator was smaller than 26 (e.g. 1/9 = [11.1%]). Placebo-side result not in abstract. 'Improvement' threshold not defined, so this is partial repigmentation, not complete coverage or colour match.

quotes.quote: Twenty-six patients were included in the study.
Colorimeter was used to assess skin colour at baseline and at 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 months of treatment.
Twenty-six patients were included in the study.
Colorimeter was used to assess skin colour at baseline and at 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 months of treatment.

Mean luminosity scale after adjusted for baseline from the treated side gradually decreased and reached statistical significance compared with the control group after 6 months of treatment (P = 0.019).
Physicians' improvement grading score showed that 11% of the patients demonstrated improvement of their skin lesions on the treated side after 6 months' treatment.
The improvements were best observed by colorimetry, yet, they were not statistically significant upon clinical assessments.

Lesions on one side of the body were selected to have a treatment with 0.1% tacrolimus ointment, whereas those on the other side served as a control with placebo ointment that had the same physical appearance.
